# `Q-25-8` — `component-props` is not a JSON object

> An element's `component-props` attribute is not a JSON object literal. The value is dropped; the component gets only the props declared in metadata.

## What this means

`component-props` carries per-element props to the component as JSON,
on top of the `props:` declared in metadata. It has to be an object
literal, for example `component-props='{"interval": 3000}'`. Any other
value (invalid JSON, an array, a bare number) is this warning, and the
attribute is dropped.

## Why this happens

- The JSON uses single quotes inside, or is missing quotes around keys.
- The attribute value was written with double quotes outside and inside
  (`component-props="{"a": 1}"`), which ends the attribute early. Use
  single quotes around the JSON.
- The value is an array or a scalar rather than an object.

## How to fix

Write the attribute as `component-props='{"key": value}'`, with the whole
JSON object in single quotes and double-quoted keys inside. For larger
payloads, build the element with `quarto.component` in a Lua filter or an
lmd cell, which encodes the props for you.
